Q: How do I get the application exit code from a Windows command line? A:

I have been using this script since DR-DOS, and of course it has changed somewhat since then.

@ECHO OFF
CLS
IF "%1" EQU "" GOTO :ERRORINPUT
SET ERROLV_TEST=%*

ECHO Testing Errorlevels:
ECHO ────────────────────
ECHO ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ECHO %ERROLV_TEST%
ECHO ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ECHO/
%ERROLV_TEST%
for %%x in (255,1,0) do if errorlevel %%x ECHO Error Code is: %%x
ECHO/
ECHO/
PAUSE
GOTO :END


:ERRORINPUT
REM Beep with BEL
ECHO • 
ECHO Error:   No parameters given
ECHO Usage:   ERRORLVL.CMD {command}
ECHO Example: ERRORLVL START /WAIT REGSVR32.EXE /S BROKEN.DLL
ECHO/
PAUSE
GOTO :END

:END
EXIT /B

EDIT:
Here is another good explanation of ERROLEVELS
https://ss64.com/nt/errorlevel.html

Q: How to model partial file promotions from a file-version SCM in Git while preserving authorship? A:

Let me see if I get it straight. So, in the non-git SCM and using your example, you can make commits of the 3 files in the feature branch and then, when merging into the upstream branch, you can choose which files you want to promote and keep the other files for later and the SCM handles that scenario fine and it is aware that the other files have not been promoted yet and at a later merge it is able to see the changes coming for those files from the commits before the first file was merged/promoted? If that is the case, in git it won't work if you mean to let git run those merges.

If you tried merging in git at a certain point and only accepted the changes for a file and discarded the changes for the other 2 files, that part (creating this commit, I mean) is good.... however, to git that commit has been merged and changes applied to the other two files before that commit that you are merging right now will not be considered in later merges (against the same upstream, of course).

However, if you are careful to replicate history of the non-git SCM on git by being extra careful to get the right content of every file in every commit (specially merge commits) that replicates the history of the non-git SCM, git should be fine to hold it and blaming files will be fine too.

You will definitely have a hard time when you start working on git and you start merging files that you had left pending to be promoted on a branch on the original SCM.... As I already explained, git won't be able to see changes from files that were not promoted but that have already been merged (commits that include those changes). You will have to be extra careful about those scenarios that might be biting your rear end. It should be happening less and less over time but it will keep on going until all of those not-yet-promoted things are finally taken care of at a later time in git merges (which will require a lot of finesse for people who are running merges to not miss any of those).... And, by the way, it will require some (non-trivial) effort to detect them using just git.... Perhaps using a separate branch to keep the yet to be promoted changes will be necessary so that those changes are not lost from sight.... In a few words: this is doable, but it will require some trickery to get right (and in a SO post I won't be able to consider all the corner cases, of course).

One overkill approach would be by keeping history of each file in their own branch and create merges each time you merge/promote files (or multiple).... Apparently merges of commits with many many parents is fine [1] so that might be the way to go. History will not be nice to look at but it should work. And, as a warning: even this approach will break if you promote/merge only certain changes from a file and keep other (committed) changes out.

[1] https://www.destroyallsoftware.com/blog/2017/the-biggest-and-weirdest-commits-in-linux-kernel-git-history

Q: Error using Material 3 TextField: "None of the following candidates is applicable" A:

The immediate problem is that you call TextField with parameters that do not exist:

  • colors is expected to be of type TextFieldColors (which is a container for multiple colors), but you provide a Color (which is only a single color)
  • The parameter Value begins with a lower case v: value = ...
  • label takes a composable function as its value, not a String. Just wrap the value in curly braces: label = { Text(on_or_off) }
  • lineLimits only exists for the TextField overload that is based on a TextFieldState. When using a String value (like you do), though, you have to use the parameter singleLine = true instead.
  • placeholder takes a composable function as its value, not a String. Just wrap the value in curly braces: placeholder = { Text(stringResource(R.string.click)) }
  • The parameter Modifier begins with a lower case m: modifier = ...
  • You are missing the required parameter onValueChange which takes a lambda that is executed every time the user changes the content of the TextField.

That said, this won't work even with all of the above fixed. For starters, the TimePickerDialog doesn't work the way you use it. It is unclear why you even want to use the android.app.TimePickerDialog from the view system when you use Compose. Mixing these is usually not a good idea. There is a TimePicker composable that you could use instead (currently in alpha, so you would need to use the alpha Compose BOM), or you could simply write your own. Furthermore, timeToShow needs to be wrapped in a MutableState, otherwise Compose won't update the UI when that variable changes. And finally, it looks like you want to use the TextField to only display a value. If you don't want the user to interact with the text then you should consider using a simple Text composable, not a TextField.

I also glanced over the rest of your code from the GitHub repository you linked. There are a lot of rather severe errors in there (like the defunct Room setup, missing/wrong coroutine handling and the leaking Context). Some of it doesn't even look salvagable. You might want to go back to the drawing board and start from scratch.

Some pointers:

  • Use a layered architecture with view models.
  • Work through the Room code labs Persist data with Room and Read and update data with Room to learn how Room should be properly used with coroutines. Make sure all your DAO functions either return a Flow or are suspending - it must be exactly one of the two.
  • For the UI, only use Material 3 Compose components, no View components like the android.app.TimePickerDialog or ConstraintLayout and so on.
  • Don't use the obsolete and buggy java.util.Calendar class, use the classes from the java.time package if you insist on using Java. Better yet, though: Kotlin has native support for Clock and Instant, and the official kotlinx-datetime library provides LocalDate and LocalDateTime, among others.
  • Never pass Context to a composable. If you need a Context, use LocalContext.current.

Q: Get start / end row when value changes A:

Here is the solution with LAG. First get the previous rank for each row. Then only keep the rows you are interested in (switch to 5 or switch from 5).

Then, I simply number these rows 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, etc. and integer-divide these row numbers by 2, so as to get group numbers 0, 1, 2, etc. For each group, the first date is the added date and the later date is the removed date.

with
  series as
  (
    select 
      ticker, rank, dt,
      lag(rank) over (partition by ticker order by dt) as prev_rank 
    from mytable
  ),
  grouped as
  (
    select
      ticker, dt,
      trunc((row_number() over (partition by ticker order by dt) - 1) / 2) as grp
    from series
    where (rank = 5 and (prev_rank <> 5 or prev_rank is null))
       or (rank <> 5 and prev_rank = 5)
  )
select ticker, min(dt) as added, max(dt) as removed
from grouped
group by ticker, grp
order by ticker, grp;

Demo: https://dbfiddle.uk/tpMm15jx

Q: Impossible to connect to a Microsoft Access database in LibreOffice 25.2 with UCanAccess and jdbcDriverOOo 1.6.2 A:

According to the docs, the url should be formatted as: jdbc:ucanaccess:///home/gouessej/Downloads/KAR.MDB

So you should probably only need to append ucanaccess: before your current connection-string.

Q: git: fatal: Could not read from remote repository A:

My issue was deploy key was already linked to my ssh key in github. I had to remove the key as a deploy key and just add the key in the main github account.
